The conveyor device comprises a conveyance element extending in a longitudinal direction between two spaced landing portions. The conveyance element is configured to transport people and/or goods from one landing portion to the other, for example in the manner of a moving walkway, escalator, or similar passenger or goods conveying system.

At least one balustrade is arranged laterally beside the conveyance element. The balustrade extends along the longitudinal direction of the conveyance element and may serve as a side boundary or support structure for the conveyor device. In particular, the balustrade can be positioned along one or both sides of the conveyance element so as to guide or separate users from adjacent areas.

The conveyor device further includes at least one sensor configured to detect the presence of a person within a defined detection zone. The detection zone is determined at least in part by the sensor’s detection direction, detection angle, and detection range. In this way, the sensor can monitor a selected area adjacent to or associated with the conveyor device and determine whether a person is present within that area.

The sensor is arranged at or next to the balustrade. Its main detection direction extends away from the balustrade, so that the sensor monitors an area outwardly from the balustrade rather than primarily along or toward the conveyance element. This arrangement enables reliable detection of persons in a defined zone beside the conveyor device, for example in an approach area, waiting area, or safety-relevant region adjacent to the balustrade.
outputs.L4:
A conveyor device for transporting people or goods between two or more landing portions includes a conveyance element, such as an escalator step band, a moving walkway belt, or a pallet chain, arranged to travel along a predetermined path between the landing portions. The conveyor device further includes at least one balustrade positioned alongside the conveyance element and extending in the direction of travel. The balustrade may support or be associated with a handrail and may define, together with the conveyance element, a passenger or load-carrying region of the conveyor device.

To improve monitoring of the conveyor device, one or more sensors are mounted on or within the balustrade. Each sensor is configured to detect the presence of a person or object within a defined detection zone located adjacent to or above the conveyance element. The detection zone may be determined by one or more parameters, including a detection direction, a detection angle, and a detection range. These parameters may be selected so that the sensor monitors a region where a person or item is likely to be present while using, entering, exiting, or standing near the conveyor device.

In particular, the sensor is oriented so that its detection direction extends away from the balustrade and toward the conveyance element, rather than along or into the balustrade itself. By directing the sensing field inwardly toward the usable transportation area, the system can more accurately identify the presence of a person or object in the relevant operating region of the conveyor device. The sensor may be configured to detect movement, proximity, distance, shape, heat, reflected light, ultrasonic signals, radar signals, or other measurable characteristics associated with a person or object.

The sensor output may be supplied to a control system of the conveyor device. Based on the detected presence or absence of a person or object in the detection zone, the control system may determine whether the conveyor device is occupied, whether a person is approaching or leaving the conveyance element, or whether an object is located in a potentially unsafe position. The control system may then adjust operation of the conveyor device, generate an alert, activate lighting or warning indicators, change speed, initiate a standby or energy-saving mode, or stop the conveyor device if a hazardous condition is detected.

The position of the sensor on the balustrade can provide a stable and advantageous mounting location while avoiding interference with the conveyance element. Because the detection zone is defined by direction, angle, and range, the sensing region can be tailored to a particular conveyor installation. For example, the sensor may be arranged to monitor a central portion of the steps or belt, an entry or exit region near a landing, or a side region where passenger behavior may require closer observation.

By directing detection away from the balustrade and toward the area used by passengers or goods, the conveyor device provides improved operational awareness. The system can distinguish relevant presence near the moving conveyance element from irrelevant structures or background surfaces, thereby enhancing detection reliability. This improved monitoring may contribute to safer operation, more responsive control, reduced energy consumption, and better management of passenger or goods movement between landing portions.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it is used to refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say **“the book,”** we are not talking about any book, but a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

“The” helps make communication clear. Without it, sentences can sound incomplete or confusing. Compare **“I saw dog”** with **“I saw the dog.”** The second sentence is more natural and tells us that the dog is known or specific.

This tiny word appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, news, instructions, and songs. It connects ideas and gives meaning to nouns. Although it is only three letters long, **“the”** plays a powerful role in making English accurate and easy to understand.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical description of an escalator or moving walkway system where sensors on the balustrade detect a person's presence, using reference numerals and formal patent language.
counterfactuals.output:
An escalator or moving walkway system 10 comprises a passenger conveying path 12 extending between a first landing region 14 and a second landing region 16. The passenger conveying path 12 is defined by a plurality of movable tread elements 18, such as escalator steps or moving-walkway pallets, coupled to and driven by a conveyor drive mechanism 20. The conveyor drive mechanism 20 may include a drive motor 22, a reduction gear assembly 24, a drive sprocket or sheave 26, and a control unit 28 configured to regulate operation of the drive motor 22.

A balustrade assembly 30 is disposed along at least one lateral side of the passenger conveying path 12. In one embodiment, the balustrade assembly 30 includes a balustrade panel 32, an inner deck portion 34, an outer deck portion 36, and a handrail guide 38 supporting a movable handrail 40. The movable handrail 40 is driven in synchronism with the tread elements 18 by a handrail drive arrangement 42.

A plurality of presence-detection sensors 50 are mounted to, embedded in, or otherwise associated with the balustrade assembly 30. The sensors 50 are arranged along a longitudinal direction of travel of the passenger conveying path 12 and are positioned to detect the presence of a person 52 adjacent to or upon the passenger conveying path 12. In one embodiment, the sensors 50 are disposed on or behind the balustrade panel 32. In another embodiment, the sensors 50 are disposed in the inner deck portion 34 or in a cover member 44 adjacent the movable handrail 40.

Each sensor 50 may comprise, by way of non-limiting example, an infrared sensor, an optical time-of-flight sensor, a capacitive proximity sensor, an ultrasonic sensor, a radar sensor, a pressure-sensitive sensor, or a combination thereof. The sensors 50 are configured to generate respective detection signals 54 indicative of the presence, absence, position, direction of movement, or dwell time of the person 52 relative to the balustrade assembly 30.

The sensors 50 are operatively connected to the control unit 28 via a communication link 56. The communication link 56 may comprise wired conductors, a field bus, a safety bus, a wireless communication channel, or a combination thereof. The control unit 28 includes a processor 58 and a memory 60 storing control instructions executable by the processor 58. Upon receipt of the detection signals 54, the control unit 28 determines whether the person 52 is entering, occupying, or leaving a detection zone 62 associated with the passenger conveying path 12.

In a standby operating mode, the drive motor 22 may be stopped or operated at a reduced speed. When at least one of the sensors 50 detects the presence of the person 52 in an approach zone 64 proximate one of the landing regions 14, 16, the control unit 28 commands the conveyor drive mechanism 20 to initiate or increase movement of the tread elements 18. The control unit 28 may further control acceleration of the drive motor 22 according to a predetermined acceleration profile to provide smooth passenger entry onto the passenger conveying path 12.

In a safety-monitoring operating mode, the control unit 28 evaluates detection signals 54 from multiple sensors 50 to identify abnormal conditions. Such abnormal conditions may include a person 52 leaning over the balustrade assembly 30, remaining stationary adjacent a landing region 14, 16 for longer than a predetermined time, moving in a direction opposite to an intended direction of travel, or entering a restricted lateral region 66 adjacent the balustrade panel 32. Upon identification of an abnormal condition, the control unit 28 may generate an alarm signal, reduce the speed of the conveyor drive mechanism 20, or actuate a braking device 68 to stop movement of the tread elements 18 and the movable handrail 40.

The sensors 50 may be arranged in sensor groups 70 corresponding to respective longitudinal segments of the balustrade assembly 30. Each sensor group 70 may define a local detection field 72 extending inwardly from the balustrade panel 32 toward the passenger conveying path 12. Adjacent detection fields 72 may overlap to provide continuous monitoring along substantially the entire length of the balustrade assembly 30. The control unit 28 may determine a travel direction of the person 52 by comparing a temporal sequence of detection signals 54 generated by adjacent sensor groups 70.

In certain embodiments, the sensors 50 are concealed behind a cover surface 74 of the balustrade assembly 30 so as not to interfere with passenger contact surfaces or the visual appearance of the escalator or moving walkway system 10. The cover surface 74 may be formed from glass, polymer, metal, or composite material selected to permit transmission of the sensing energy used by the sensors 50.

The presence-detection sensors 50 may further be connected to a safety circuit 80 independent of the primary control unit 28. The safety circuit 80 may include redundant input channels 82, 84 and a safety controller 86 configured to compare sensor outputs and detect faults such as open circuits, short circuits, signal disagreement, or sensor failure. Upon detection of a fault or unsafe condition, the safety controller 86 actuates the braking device 68 or interrupts power supplied to the drive motor 22.

Accordingly, the escalator or moving walkway system 10 provides balustrade-mounted presence detection for automatic starting, speed regulation, passenger-flow monitoring, and safety supervision, while maintaining the sensors 50 in positions protected from direct passenger impact and environmental contamination.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for detecting passengers on a people conveyor, specifying that the sensor is positioned at or next to the balustrade and points away from it.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is provided for detecting passengers on a people conveyor, such as an escalator or moving walkway.

The people conveyor includes a conveyor path for transporting passengers and at least one balustrade arranged along a side of the conveyor path. A passenger-detection sensor is mounted at, on, in, or next to the balustrade. The sensor is oriented so that its detection direction points away from the balustrade and toward the passenger-carrying region of the conveyor.

In use, the sensor emits or receives a detection signal across or into the conveyor path to determine whether a passenger is present on the moving steps, pallets, or belt. Because the sensor is positioned at or adjacent to the balustrade and directed away from it, the sensor can monitor the occupied region of the conveyor without requiring installation in the floor or in the moving conveyor elements.

The sensor may be an optical sensor, infrared sensor, time-of-flight sensor, ultrasonic sensor, radar sensor, camera-based sensor, or another proximity or presence-detection device. The detected passenger information may be supplied to a controller of the people conveyor, for example to start, stop, slow, accelerate, illuminate, or otherwise control operation of the conveyor based on passenger presence.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
